query_text: For every warehouse, as of March 31, 2025, report the number of active SKUs whose latest recorded stock is positive and the total known on-hand units for active SKUs. Use the latest snapshot per warehouse and SKU at or before the end of that day.
reference_sql: WITH ranked_snapshots AS (SELECT i.warehouse_id, i.sku_id, i.on_hand_qty, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.warehouse_id, i.sku_id ORDER BY i.snapshot_at DESC, i.snapshot_id DESC) AS rn FROM inventory_snapshots AS i WHERE i.snapshot_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00'), latest AS (SELECT warehouse_id, sku_id, on_hand_qty FROM ranked_snapshots WHERE rn = 1) SELECT w.warehouse_id, w.warehouse_name, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.lifecycle_status = 'active' AND l.on_hand_qty > 0) AS active_skus_with_positive_stock, COALESCE(SUM(l.on_hand_qty) FILTER (WHERE p.lifecycle_status = 'active' AND l.on_hand_qty IS NOT NULL), 0) AS known_active_on_hand_units FROM warehouses AS w LEFT JOIN latest AS l ON l.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id LEFT JOIN products AS p ON p.sku_id = l.sku_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.warehouse_name ORDER BY w.warehouse_id;
database_schema: CREATE TABLE warehouses (warehouse_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, warehouse_name TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE products (sku_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, sku_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, lifecycle_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (lifecycle_status IN ('active', 'discontinued'))); CREATE TABLE inventory_snapshots (snapshot_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, warehouse_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES warehouses(warehouse_id), sku_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES products(sku_id), snapshot_at TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE NOT NULL, on_hand_qty NUMERIC(14,3));
business_context: Snapshot timestamps are stored in UTC. If two snapshots for the same warehouse and SKU have the same timestamp, the higher snapshot_id is the authoritative one. A null on_hand_qty means the latest quantity is unknown; it must not be replaced by an older snapshot. All warehouses remain in the output, including those without a qualifying snapshot.
failure_mechanism: Summing snapshot history instead of selecting the latest row per warehouse and SKU counts historical quantities repeatedly. Treating a null latest quantity as zero or falling back to an older value also misstates the reported stock.
business_grain_note: First reduce snapshot history to one row per warehouse and SKU, then aggregate active SKUs and known quantities at the warehouse grain. The ranking tie-breaker makes the selected row deterministic.
missing_value_handling: A null quantity in the latest snapshot is unknown and is excluded from both the positive-SKU count and known-units sum. No snapshot contributes no known quantity; the displayed zero total does not assert that physical inventory is zero.
temporal_boundary_rule: Include snapshots strictly before 2025-04-01 00:00:00 UTC, which includes the full day of March 31. Rank only snapshots within this as-of boundary.

query_text: For each supplier with at least one late purchase order, count purchase orders whose promised delivery date falls in the first quarter of 2025. Exclude cancelled orders. Treat an order as late if any receipt was recorded after its promised date, and count each order once.
reference_sql: SELECT s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name, COUNT(*) AS late_purchase_order_count FROM suppliers AS s JOIN purchase_orders AS po ON po.supplier_id = s.supplier_id WHERE po.status <> 'cancelled' AND po.promised_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND po.promised_date < DATE '2025-04-01' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM receipt_events AS r WHERE r.purchase_order_id = po.purchase_order_id AND r.received_date > po.promised_date) GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name ORDER BY s.supplier_id;
database_schema: CREATE TABLE suppliers (supplier_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, supplier_name TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE purchase_orders (purchase_order_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, supplier_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES suppliers(supplier_id), promised_date DATE, status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('open', 'received', 'cancelled'))); CREATE TABLE receipt_events (receipt_event_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, purchase_order_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES purchase_orders(purchase_order_id), received_date DATE);
business_context: A purchase order is late if at least one receipt event has a non-null received date strictly later than the promised date. Orders with no promised date cannot be assigned to the quarter and are excluded. The reporting period is the first calendar quarter of 2025.
failure_mechanism: Joining purchase orders directly to receipt events can produce multiple rows for one order and inflate the count. EXISTS tests whether a late receipt exists without changing the purchase-order grain.
business_grain_note: The counted entity is a purchase order, not a receipt event. The supplier-level count therefore includes each qualifying order once, regardless of how many receipt events it has.
missing_value_handling: A null promised date is excluded by the quarter filter. A null received date does not satisfy the strict late-date comparison and is not treated as late.
temporal_boundary_rule: The promised-date window is half-open: January 1, 2025 is included and April 1, 2025 is excluded. A receipt is late only when received_date is strictly greater than promised_date.

query_text: For each supplier with outstanding purchase-order lines, report the number of lines and total units still outstanding for orders placed during calendar year 2025, as of the end of December 31, 2025. Exclude cancelled orders and do not report lines with no remaining quantity.
reference_sql: WITH receipt_totals AS (SELECT r.line_id, SUM(r.received_qty) AS received_qty FROM receipt_events AS r WHERE r.received_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY r.line_id), line_balances AS (SELECT po.supplier_id, pol.line_id, GREATEST(pol.ordered_qty - COALESCE(rt.received_qty, 0), 0) AS outstanding_qty FROM purchase_orders AS po JOIN purchase_order_lines AS pol ON pol.purchase_order_id = po.purchase_order_id LEFT JOIN receipt_totals AS rt ON rt.line_id = pol.line_id WHERE po.status <> 'cancelled' AND po.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND po.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00') SELECT s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name, COUNT(lb.line_id) AS outstanding_line_count, SUM(lb.outstanding_qty) AS outstanding_units FROM line_balances AS lb JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplier_id = lb.supplier_id WHERE lb.outstanding_qty > 0 GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name ORDER BY s.supplier_id;
database_schema: CREATE TABLE suppliers (supplier_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, supplier_name TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE purchase_orders (purchase_order_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, supplier_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES suppliers(supplier_id), placed_at TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('open', 'partially_received', 'cancelled'))); CREATE TABLE purchase_order_lines (line_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, purchase_order_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES purchase_orders(purchase_order_id), ordered_qty NUMERIC(14,3) NOT NULL CHECK (ordered_qty >= 0)); CREATE TABLE receipt_events (receipt_event_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, line_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES purchase_order_lines(line_id), received_at TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE NOT NULL, received_qty NUMERIC(14,3) NOT NULL CHECK (received_qty >= 0));
business_context: The reporting period and as-of cutoff use UTC timestamps. Apply all receipt events recorded before 2026-01-01 00:00:00 to their purchase-order lines. Missing receipt rows mean no units have been received. If receipts exceed the ordered quantity, outstanding quantity is zero rather than negative.
failure_mechanism: Joining each purchase-order line directly to its receipt events repeats the line for every event, inflating line counts and potentially duplicating ordered quantities. Aggregate receipts to one total per line before calculating outstanding units.
business_grain_note: Compute remaining quantity at the purchase-order-line grain after aggregating receipts by line, then count outstanding lines and sum their balances at the supplier grain. Receipt events are not the reporting entity.
missing_value_handling: The left join preserves lines without receipt events; COALESCE treats their missing receipt total as zero received. The schema disallows null ordered and received quantities. GREATEST prevents over-receipts from creating negative outstanding units.
temporal_boundary_rule: Include orders placed from 2025-01-01 00:00:00 UTC up to, but not including, 2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. Count receipt events recorded before the same exclusive cutoff, including events on December 31.
